n: The speaker—the prophet, or the Lord Himself—vows not to keep quiet or rest until Zion’s righteousness shines like dawn and her salvation blazes like a torch.

f.w: For Zion's sake will I not hold my peace

n: Nations and kings will see her glory, and the Lord Himself will give her a new name. In scripture a new name marks a new identity and covenant relationship.

f.w: thou shalt be called by a new name

n: Zion will be a beautiful crown held in God’s hand—His treasured, honored possession.
No longer called “Forsaken” or “Desolate,” Zion will be named Hephzibah, “My delight is in her,” and her land Beulah, “Married.” The covenant relationship is restored like a joyful marriage.

f.g: Hebrew: “My delight is in her.” Also the name of Hezekiah’s wife (2 Kings 21:1).

n: As a young man marries a bride, so Zion’s children will claim her, and as a groom rejoices over his bride, God will rejoice over His people.

f.w: as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride

n: God has posted watchmen on Jerusalem’s walls who pray day and night without stopping. Those who “remind” the Lord in prayer must not be silent.

f.w: I have set watchmen upon thy walls
ye that make mention of the LORD
f.g: Those who call on the Lord or remind Him in prayer—intercessors.

n: Give the Lord no rest until He establishes Jerusalem and makes her the praise of the earth. A bold invitation to persistent prayer.
God swears by His powerful right arm that enemies will no longer seize Israel’s grain or foreigners drink her wine.

f.w: The LORD hath sworn by his right hand

n: Those who harvest will eat and praise the Lord, and those who gather grapes will drink in the courts of His sanctuary—celebrating festivals in peace.
Go out through the gates! Build the road for the people, clear the stones, and raise a banner for the nations. The way home for God’s people is being prepared.

f.w: cast up, cast up the highway
lift up a standard for the people

n: The Lord has announced to the whole world: tell Zion, your salvation is coming, bringing His reward with Him. In Hebrew “salvation” is yeshu‘ah, closely related to the name Jesus (Yeshua).

f.g: Hebrew yesha‘ / yeshu‘ah—close to the name Yeshua (Jesus).

n: God’s people will be called “The Holy People” and “The Redeemed of the Lord,” and Zion will be called “Sought Out” and “A City Not Forsaken.” She who felt abandoned is now pursued by God’s love.
